question: Which of the following gases is evolved when dilute hydrochloric acid reacts with sodium hydrogencarbonate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Carbon dioxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• When dilute **hydrochloric acid (HCl)** reacts with **sodium hydrogencarbonate (NaHCO₃)**, the reaction produces **carbon dioxide gas (CO₂)**, along with water (H₂O) and sodium chloride (NaCl).
 
• The chemical reaction for this process is: NaHCO₃ + HCl → NaCl + H₂O + CO₂. This is a classic acid-carbonate reaction where carbon dioxide gas is released.
 
• The evolution of carbon dioxide can be observed as effervescence or bubbling during the reaction.
 
• This reaction is commonly used in experiments to demonstrate the presence of carbon dioxide, as the gas can turn limewater (Ca(OH)₂) milky when bubbled through it, due to the formation of calcium carbonate (CaCO₃).
 
• None of the other options (Nitrogen, Oxygen, or Hydrogen) is evolved in this reaction. The reaction specifically releases carbon dioxide due to the decomposition of the bicarbonate ion (HCO3<
